title: Web development
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Build web applications: how the web works, semantic and accessible HTML, CSS layout and responsive design, JavaScript, the DOM and events, asynchronous code with promises and fetch, REST APIs and JSON, server-side development in Python with Flask, databases, templates and forms, authentication, sessions and web security, and testing and deployment.
primary_reading: MDN Web Docs: Learn web development (free)

weeks.1: How the web works: HTTP, URLs and browsers
weeks.3: CSS: the box model and selectors
weeks.4: Layout: flexbox, grid and responsive design
weeks.7: Asynchronous JavaScript: promises, async and fetch
weeks.9: Server-side web development with Python and Flask

blocks.deliverable: Write an accessible page with semantic HTML.
Week 7 midterm; fetch and display data from a public API.
Build a small server with routes and a database.
Add sign-in and fix a security bug.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Full-stack application: design and build a small web app (for example a reading tracker or an event board) with a responsive, accessible front end, a Flask REST API, a database, sign-in, tests and deployment instructions, plus an accessibility and security checklist.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
